# Research log

2026-11-12 23:17 +04 — Stronger result found: the third and fourth centered moments for S and C can also be transferred. Their normalized third moment is a₃=κ/ζ(2)−2J₃/(3ζ(2)³), where J₃=∫H(x)³ν(dx)=6ζ(4)−3ζ(3)−(3/2)ζ(2). Since J₃≤log(2)∫H²ν, a₃>0. Fourth moments are bounded (in fact converge to the fixed-point prediction), so cubic moments are uniformly integrable. Therefore neither standardized Sackin nor standardized Colless can converge to a Gaussian. A full limit theorem is proved for QC; existence/uniqueness of the Sackin fixed-point law remains to be established unless a further argument is found.

2026-11-12 23:17 +04 — Literature limitation: the two supplied texts are AJ and BCM, not the Iksanov–Nikitin–Yakymiv paper. Neither includes arXiv:2510.17343 or those three authors together. AJ discusses earlier Iksanov leaf-height results in §3.5. The specific 2510.17343 assertion therefore cannot be independently checked from the supplied material; it will be marked citation to check. BCM's relevant theorems and its uses of Proposition 1.3 have been read.

Timestamp correction (2026-11-12 23:13 +04): the initial manually stamped 23:12 entries below were written about 23:09. Subsequent program entries use the machine clock.

2026-11-12 23:13 +04 — Proved the outline for all three variance constants: Sackin and Colless share κ=(2ζ(3)−ζ(2))/ζ(2)²=0.280574126406891865... at scale n²log²n; QC constant is 2/11 at scale n⁴log²n. For S, an elementary defect computation gives mean n[(log n)²/(2ζ(2))+(γ/ζ(2)+ζ(3)/ζ(2)²)log n]+O(n), avoiding dependence on an imported high-order expansion. For D=S−C, the same argument gives mean (2log2/ζ(2))n log n+O(n) and Var D=O(n²log n), sufficient for the common leading variance and joint asymptotic equality. Detailed endpoint bounds and proofs to be audited in REPORT.md.

2026-11-12 23:13 +04 — First launch encountered sandbox refusal of nice and macOS rejection of RLIMIT_AS. No privileged retry. The launcher already requests nice 10; all programs set numerical thread environment variables before importing NumPy. Using RSS checks and explicit array-size bounds instead. NumPy longdouble on this ARM machine has only 52 mantissa bits, so the independent Decimal-45 computation, not the dtype name, supplies high-precision verification.

2026-11-12 23:13 +04 — Full PMFs are being computed without tail truncation. Small PMFs independently agree with exact rational convolution through n=12. NumPy matmul emits spurious floating-point status warnings while returning finite verified values; replace these diagnostic dot products by scalar elementwise reductions on the next audit. Convolution moment checks so far remain within about 10^−12 relative error through n=200 for S and C.

Task received: 2026-11-12, approximately 23:06 Asia/Tbilisi. Study distributions of Sackin, Colless and quadratic Colless for DTCS(n), Open Problem 10.

2026-11-12 23:07 +04 — Started in P0347. Only the two supplied paper texts and launcher files are present. All writes, programs, results and coordination records will stay here, as specifically requested; no external brain/mesh/checklist mutation, agents, pushes, or visible windows. Governor read-only check reports owner away, CPU saturation warning, no distress. Computations will run at nice 10 with one numerical-library thread and a per-process memory guard.

2026-11-12 23:07 +04 — Text search locates the overview's claim c(m) ~ m/2 at line 3147. BCM explicitly describes Proposition 1.3 as a linear-mean, linear-variance CLT; its hypotheses and the relevant sections are being read in full. No occurrence of Sackin or Colless in that text.

2026-11-12 23:12 +04 — Read overview §§4.7–4.9.2 and BCM introduction through §1.4. Overview also claims g(m) ~ m²/4. Both toll claims are wrong for the stated q: E[I(m−I)]=m(m−1)/(2h), hence g(m)=m²−2m(m−1)/h ~ m²; and E min(I,m−I)=O(m/h), hence c(m)~m. BCM Corollary 1.5 concerns total continuous-time tree length, not Sackin. Proposition 1.3 permits dependence between I and b, so random Colless toll is allowed, but linear mean/variance and small third toll moment must still hold.

2026-11-12 23:12 +04 — Analytic route found for QC: for p>1, the binary recursion defect of n^p(log n)^r is asymptotic to H_{p−1} n^p(log n)^r/h (integer p). Positivity barriers transfer toll asymptotics. This suggests E QC~n²log n, Var QC~(2/11)n⁴log² n and a positive non-Gaussian moment-determined limit. Proof and independent numerical verification pending.

2026-11-12T23:29:14+04:00 — Second analytic derivation of the QC variance constant found: the explicit defect of n² log n gives E QC=n² log n+O(n²). Its centered root toll is -2n² log n x(1-x)+O(n²), whose second moment is asymptotic to n⁴ log n/3. The variance recursion divides by psi(4)=11/6, independently giving 2/11.
